title: Frequency-Domain Multi-Modality Transportation Modeling

problem.claim: Accurate forecasting for coupled transportation modalities is challenging because the modalities have distinct spectral characteristics and uneven cross-frequency interactions.

gap.claim: Most existing methods operate primarily in the time domain or rely on coarse feature fusion.

contributions.claim: FreMo is a frequency-domain model for adaptive and selective cross-modality synergy in multi-modality transportation forecasting.
FreMo decouples spectral refinement by modality from cross-modality synergy and can be integrated as a plug-and-play component with general time-series backbones.
FreMo includes a Modality-Wise Frequency Filter for adaptive within-modality spectral refinement and a Frequency-Guided Synergy Integrator for selective cross-modality aggregation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world datasets reportedly show that FreMo consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines.
The authors report superior performance and generalization across diverse forecasting scenarios.
The code is reported as available at the supplied repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multi-modality transportation systems contain coupled transportation modes with shared temporal patterns.
Forecasting is difficult because modalities differ spectrally and interact unevenly across frequencies, while existing methods use time-domain modeling or coarse fusion.
FreMo addresses the limitations through frequency-domain modeling with adaptive and selective cross-modality synergy.
MFF refines modality-specific spectral components, while FSI selectively aggregates cross-modality information by frequency.
Experiments reportedly show improved performance and generalization across diverse forecasting scenarios, and code is available.

source_observation.claim: Separating modality-specific spectral refinement from frequency-dependent cross-modality aggregation is presented as the core modeling strategy.

interpretation.claim: When heterogeneous signals differ in frequency behavior, separate denoising or refinement from selective information sharing may reduce negative transfer.

application.claim: This strategy may be applicable to other multi-modal time-series forecasting settings with heterogeneous spectral characteristics.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the strategy generalizes beyond the reported transportation forecasting scenarios.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the forecasting horizons, modality configurations, or backbone implementations.
The abstract does not provide details sufficient to assess computational cost or reproducibility.
